events.did: said his name in the dark and sat upright in their bed, waking him
events.quote_anchor: “Gabe.” A tense exhale, whispered in the dark. He dragged himself from sleep to find Iris sitting upright in their bed, sheets clutched against her chest.

events.did: told Iris to go to Ian's room and lock the door
events.quote_anchor: “It’s all right,” he said steadily. “Go to Ian’s room. Lock the door.”

events.did: slammed his hands down on the desk, showing that Gabriel's notebook had been torn open and a dozen pages torn out
events.quote_anchor: His patient slammed his hands down on the desk, and Gabriel saw the notebook—his notebook—disemboweled, a dozen pages torn out.

events.did: told Gabriel that his sister Sarah showed up and he told her she could stay
events.quote_anchor: The air shuddered in his chest. “My sister, Sarah, showed up. I told her she could stay.”

events.did: described finding Sarah on the floor, full of holes and ripped up like she was made of paper
events.quote_anchor: She was on the floor. And she was full of holes. Ripped up. Like, like she was made of paper.

events.did: filled the syringe from the vial with a lethal dose, saying he just wanted to sleep
events.quote_anchor: “I just want to sleep.” His hands were shaking as he filled the syringe. A lethal dose.

events.did: slammed Paul's wrist against the desk to knock the hypodermic from his hand, and Paul struck his head on the desk corner
events.quote_anchor: He slammed Paul’s wrist against the desk, knocking the hypodermic from his hand.

events.did: was buried with Iris and Ian when the roof caved in and the stairs gave way
events.quote_anchor: But then the roof caved in, and the stairs gave way, and the last thing Gabriel felt was her fingers skimming his

relations.did: is Paul Barnett's therapist and runs biweekly sessions with him
relations.quote_anchor: Over the course of their biweekly sessions, Paul had only mentioned his family once—his grandparents, dead, his parents, estranged.
“My sister, Sarah, showed up. I told her she could stay.”

relations.did: carries Ian down the stairs toward Gabriel in the collapsing house
relations.quote_anchor: There she was, at the top of the stairs, Ian cradled against her side, their faces twin masks of shock, and fear.

relations.did: accuses Gabriel of lying to him and of letting him think his condition was all in his head
relations.quote_anchor: “You let me think it was all in my head. You let me think I was safe.”

numbers.did: there were twenty-eight steps between Dr. Gray's office and Gabriel's home
numbers.quote_anchor: There were twenty-eight steps between Dr. Gray’s office and Gabriel’s home, but he couldn’t make them fast enough.

numbers.did: a dozen pages were torn out of Gabriel's notebook
numbers.quote_anchor: His patient slammed his hands down on the desk, and Gabriel saw the notebook—his notebook—disemboweled, a dozen pages torn out.

numbers.did: the last two months had promised so much more
numbers.quote_anchor: But the last two months had promised so much more.

numbers.did: five steps from the office to the bottom of the stairs, where there should have been twelve up
numbers.quote_anchor: Five from the office to the bottom of the stairs, what should have been twelve up, but as his foot hit the fifth, the step beneath him broke.

numbers.did: counted eleven down and seventeen from the door
numbers.quote_anchor: Eleven down, and seventeen … seventeen … but that was from the door.
